items.text: Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Jayden Reed (GB) will have neck surgery and miss the rest of 2026, and Reed went on injured reserve the same day. An IR slot buys nothing in a redraft league now, and nobody inherits his job: the third receiver vs ATL was a three-man rotation, Skyy Moore 27 routes, J. Michael Sturdivant 19 and Bo Melton 19 on 55 dropbacks. Drop Reed in every redraft format.

Nico Collins (HOU) practiced Wednesday as a limited participant, his first session since the hamstring strain that cost him Weeks 2 and 3, and DeMeco Ryans is hopeful he plays vs DAL. He stays WR15 on the Menu with the Q flag, and Dallas has allowed 7 passing touchdowns in three games. Monitor Collins; Thursday's practice and Friday's designation decide it.

The Menu had David Montgomery (HOU) as an RB2 start off one game, 34 snaps to Woody Marks' 20 vs IND. Over three games the snaps are close to even: about level in Week 1, 42 to 38 in Week 2, then 34 to 20. Montgomery is at 2.8 yards a carry and has been hit at or behind the line on 68 percent of his runs, the highest rate in the league. Marks has more targets, 8 to 7. Both Menu lists now read the same. Flex Montgomery vs DAL; he is not an RB2 this week.

Woody Marks (HOU) has 8 targets and 50 routes in three games, and 37 percent of the snaps was Week 3 only; the split was about even in Week 1 and 42 to 38 in Week 2. His role grows when Houston trails, 6 targets in the 20-6 loss to CIN, and he took the goal-line score at IND. Flex him vs DAL in PPR.

The Menu had Daniel Jones (IND) as a sit in London with Josh Downs and Tyler Warren as the whole tree. Keenan Allen had 9 targets too: Downs 11, Warren 10 and Allen 9 took 30 of the 36 attempts vs HOU. Washington has allowed 280.3 passing yards a game, 31st in the league, and a league-high 11 passing touchdowns in three games. Stream Jones vs WAS in London.

Brian Thomas Jr. (JAX) ran 13 to 15 routes vs NE, under half of the dropbacks, on 23 of 62 snaps; he was on the field for 77 percent of the three-receiver snaps and off it in two-tight-end sets. Rookie Josh Cameron matched his 23 snaps and scored. The Menu had Thomas as a flex while the Market Run and Heat Check said drop; the Menu row now reads sit. Sit him @CIN, and in 12-team leagues cut him for any add on the Market Run list.

Jake Ferguson (DAL) is TE15 on the Menu and the row now reads sit instead of stream. His snap share went 76, 60 and 69 percent by week while Brevyn Spann-Ford went 22, 38 and 38, he is fifth on his own team with 11 targets, and he lost a fumble on the opening drive vs BAL. The 3 touchdowns are the whole line, and the Butcher Shop already has him as a sell. Sit him @HOU for any tight end with a steadier target share.

Javonte Williams (DAL) had 19 carries for 98 and a touchdown on 56 snaps, 76 percent, vs BAL, and the Menu row said every touch was his with Malik Davis hurt. Tyler Goodson made his Dallas debut as the No. 2 with 11 snaps and 6 carries for 22, and Emari Demercado did not play a snap. The role is the same; the name behind him changed. Start Williams as your RB2 @HOU.

The Menu's Bo Nix (DEN) note leaned on a rushing floor that has not shown up: 12 carries for 15 yards in three games, with one 1-yard touchdown vs LAR. San Francisco is without Nick Bosa and several defensive linemen, and Arizona ran 87 plays and scored 30 on that front in Week 3, so it is not the tough spot the note called it. Nix is 56 of 93 for 605 yards, 4 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Stream him @SF.

The Menu's Matthew Golden (GB) row said Jayden Reed's absence gives him the routes. He already had them: an 83 percent route share, 25 percent of the targets and 40 percent of the air yards through three games, two of them with Reed active, for 15 catches, 253 yards and a touchdown. Vs ATL he ran 44 routes on 55 dropbacks and drew 12 targets. Start him as your WR2 @TB.

C.J. Stroud (HOU) stays a streamer on the Menu, and the note is fixed. Nico Collins was limited Wednesday, his first practice since the hamstring. Dallas has allowed two or more passing touchdowns in all three games, 7 total, lost two defensive backs in Rio and left three more at home. Stroud went 16 of 27 for 167 and a touchdown at IND without Collins. Stream him vs DAL; he moves up the list if Collins is cleared Friday.

Keenan Allen (IND) faces possible league discipline after a September charge from an August arrest; league policy carries a three-game minimum, none has been announced, the next court date is Oct 26 and he is eligible now. He has 20 targets on 75 routes, 26.7 percent, and took 9 of 36 attempts vs HOU. Claim him, 3 to 6 percent of FAAB, and know a ban could land in season.

The Market Run said most of Xavier Worthy's (KC) snaps come without a route. Kansas City had 24 dropbacks on 49 plays @MIA, and his 19 routes are a 79 percent route share, level with Travis Kelce and one more than Rashee Rice. The routes are there; 63 yards on 15 targets in three games with no game above 25 is the problem. Drop him for Sadiq, Harris or Keenan Allen.

The Menu's Kenneth Walker III (KC) note counted three scores vs MIA. He scored twice: 18 for 70 and a rushing touchdown plus a 5-yard receiving touchdown, on 73 percent of the snaps with 18 of the 24 running back carries. Start him as your RB1 @LV.

Ben Johnson said Tuesday that Tyson Bagent (CHI) starts vs NYJ if he gets a full week of first-team practice; Bagent missed the Week 3 start only because the concussion protocol cost him practice time, and no starter is officially named. Every Week 3 target share (Luther Burden III 32 percent, Kalif Raymond 21 percent) was built with Case Keenum. Leave both quarterbacks on waivers; monitor the first-team reps through Friday and the Friday designation.
items.watch: first-team reps through Friday and the Friday designation

items.text: Khalil Shakir (BUF) drew 3 targets and caught 1 for 6 yards on 73 percent of the snaps vs LAC while DJ Moore drew a team-high 10. The Menu row said the volume was coming his way; it did not. Sit him vs NE; he comes down the receiver list on Friday's Prep Notes.

Quinshon Judkins (CLE) has 42 carries for 124 yards, 3.0 a carry, and no touchdown through three games, and his 18 carries for 70 in Week 3 came vs CAR, not PIT, which the Menu row now says. He ran 11 routes to Raheim Sanders' 16, and center Elgton Jenkins (concussion) is expected out Thursday with Luke Wypler starting. Flex him vs PIT on Thursday, nothing more, on both Menu lists.

DJ Moore (BUF) led Buffalo with 10 targets and caught 6 for 67 on 64 percent of the snaps through the shoulder vs LAC. His Menu rows now carry the targets and agree with each other: start him as a WR3 vs NE, and he is a flex, not a sit, on the flex list.

James Cook (BUF) ran 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown on 67 percent of the snaps and 81 percent of the early downs vs LAC, with 1 target and no catch, while Ty Johnson came back and took the passing downs (15 snaps, 4 of 4 for 50). The Menu note that pinned more handoffs on Allen's knee is gone; the carries are the reason. Start Cook as your RB1 vs NE and expect the catches to stay with Johnson.

Lamar Jackson (BAL) was not at the start of Wednesday's practice minutes after his press conference, with no injury or illness given, and he spoke as if he plays vs TEN. Both centers, Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and Ethan Pocic (knee), are out longer term, so rookie guard Vega Ioane starts at center with Andrew Vorhees at right guard. He stays QB2 on the Menu; monitor Thursday's practice report, and start him if he is on it.

Derrick Henry (BAL) ran 26 times for 89 yards (3.4) and 2 touchdowns vs DAL on 67 percent of the snaps, with his 11 inside runs going for 23 yards and two stops on fourth-and-1, and now both centers are out. He has 6 touchdowns in three games and the goal line is still his. Start him as your RB1 vs TEN; the line is why the yardage floor is lower than the rank.

Left guard Damien Lewis (CAR) has a UCL tear in his elbow and is out vs DET, so Corey Bullock makes his first start and Carolina has three backup linemen in front of Bryce Young, the most-pressured quarterback in the league at 47 percent of dropbacks. Young had his foot stepped on at CLE, did not miss a snap, and Dave Canales expects him to play. He stays QB12 on the Menu with 939 passing yards behind him; monitor Thursday and Friday practice for his foot and for Jalen Coker before you commit.
items.watch: Thursday and Friday practice for Young's foot and for Coker

items.text: Head coach Joe Brady said again Wednesday that he is not concerned about Josh Allen's (BUF) left knee after the fourth-quarter hit vs LAC; the Monday 'a little sore' line was Brady's, not the offensive coordinator's, and the Menu row now says so. Allen played all 66 snaps and has multiple rushing touchdowns in three straight games. Start him as your QB1 vs NE.

Mark Andrews (BAL) was not among the players missing Wednesday's practice after the hand injury in Brazil, and his 33 of 64 snaps were an even split with Durham Smythe, which reads like the role, not the hand. He had 5 targets and 3 for 24. Stream him vs TEN if you need a tight end; he is TE14 on the Menu, not a weekly start.

Kyle Pitts (ATL) has 6 targets in three games (1, 3, 2) for 2 catches and 20 yards, and at GB with Michael Penix Jr. he caught 1 of 2 for 5 on 19 routes while playing fewer snaps than Charlie Woerner. The Menu row said 3 targets; the count is 6, and the call is the same. Sit him at NO; he needs a 5-target game before he is a streamer.

Chuba Hubbard (CAR) had 19 carries for 82 yards and 4 catches on 4 targets for 28 on 65 of 77 snaps (84 percent) at CLE, with AJ Dillon at 4 carries and 12 snaps; the Menu had 20 carries, and the row, the flex row, the Special and the intro now say 19. His snap share has gone 71, 65, 84 percent by week. Start him as your RB2 vs DET on Sunday night.

Jeremiyah Love (ARI) out-snapped Tyler Allgeier for the first time in Week 3, 56 snaps (64 percent) to 31, after Allgeier led 60 to 43 percent in Weeks 1 and 2: 21 of the backs' 23 carries for 90, 5 of 5 targets for 19 and a receiving touchdown, 22 routes. Allgeier kept 3 of the 5 goal-line snaps, and the game was a 54-dropback trailing script. Start Love as your RB2 @NYG and watch the first-half split and the goal line.

Harold Fannin Jr. (CLE) drew 9 targets, a 30 percent share, with 45 percent of the air yards, 7 catches for 51 and 2 touchdowns vs CAR on 87 percent of the snaps and 77 percent of the routes; his targets have gone 3, 6, 9 by week. Jerry Jeudy ran 23 routes with no target. Start Fannin as your TE1 vs PIT on Thursday.

Zay Flowers (BAL) practiced Wednesday, his first session of TEN week, after 21 snaps and 15 routes in Brazil. On 26 routes this season he has 234 yards and a target on 48 percent of them, both league highs among players with 25 or more routes. Start him as your WR1 vs TEN; the game is in Baltimore.

Darren Waller (CAR) led Carolina with 8 targets on 28 routes and 39 of 77 snaps at CLE, 5 catches for 51, and his snaps have gone 24, 29, 39 by week with Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out. He is outside the Menu's top 20 tight ends, so this is a streamer's call. Monitor Coker's Friday designation; stream Waller vs DET if Coker is out, and sit him if Coker plays.
items.watch: Jalen Coker's Friday designation; stream Waller vs DET if Coker is out

items.text: Kalif Raymond (CHI) has 23 percent of the targets on 66 percent of the routes and 214 receiving yards through three games, with 9 or more PPR points in each, on more than 60 percent of the snaps every week. The usage is real; the quarterback may change to Tyson Bagent, and the share was built with Case Keenum. Add him in PPR, 2 to 5 percent of FAAB, as a WR4 with a floor, not a starter until you see him with Bagent.

Klint Kubiak said Monday that Mike Washington Jr. (LV) earned more opportunities, the second time he has said it. Ashton Jeanty's last 40 carries went for 104 yards, he visited the trainers @NO, and he still has 63 of the two backs' 78 carries (81 percent) and all 16 targets. The Butcher Shop card keeps the trade-for call with the first-half carry split vs KC as the check. Trade for him; offer a low-end WR1 or a RB1 whose role is less secure.
items.price: a low-end WR1 or a RB1 with a shakier role

items.text: Mike Washington Jr. (LV) has 15 carries for 102 yards, 6.8 a carry, with 5 for 54 and a 36-yard touchdown @NO, and the coach has said twice that he earned more opportunities. He has no receiving role. Jeanty still has 81 percent of the backs' carries, so this is a handcuff with a rising early-down share, and the yards per carry back it. Stash him, 3 to 8 percent of FAAB, if you own Jeanty or have a deep bench.

The Menu had Colston Loveland (CHI) at 4 of 4 for 34 yards vs PHI; the game line was 31, and 34 is his season total on 5 catches. His target share is 10 percent on 71 percent of the routes this season. Kalif Raymond has 23 percent of the targets. Loveland's row keeps its number and its call. Start him as your TE1 vs NYJ.

Carolina placed both starting corners on injured reserve Wednesday, Jaycee Horn (quad) and Mike Jackson (groin), so rookie Will Lee III, Akayleb Evans and Chau Smith-Wade are the corners for Sunday night vs DET. Jared Goff (DET) is the Menu's stream of the week, and every Detroit pass catcher moved up on the page this morning. Stream Goff at CAR.

John Harbaugh said Jameis Winston starts vs ARI and that J.J. McCarthy, acquired from MIN for a 2027 fifth-round pick, is the No. 2 or 3 while he learns the offense. Malik Nabers (NYG) drew 27 percent of the targets in Winston's first start but caught 5 of 6 for 26 yards at an average depth of target of 1.0. Hold Nabers as a WR2 on volume; what changes the call is McCarthy taking the job, and Week 6 vs NO is the first realistic date for that.
items.why: 27 percent of the targets holds even with a 1.0 average depth of target; the call changes only if McCarthy takes the job, Week 6 vs NO at the earliest.

items.text: Tampa Bay put Jalen McMillan (TB) on injured reserve Wednesday with the PCL strain, designated to return, 6 to 8 weeks per the reporting. Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin are the whole receiver room with an undrafted rookie at quarterback; Egbuka is a WR3 on this week's Menu and Godwin a flex. Drop McMillan unless you have an IR slot.

Rico Dowdle (PIT) is a non-participant on Wednesday's estimated report, his third straight DNP on the short week, and he has not practiced since the toe injury in Week 2. Jaylen Warren played 90 percent of the snaps and touched the ball 20 times without him, and he is RB10 on this week's Menu. Start Warren as your RB1 @CLE Thursday night.

Rachaad White (WAS) sat out Wednesday's session in London with the shoulder he hurt vs SEA, and Dan Quinn says he is getting treatment. White played 43 percent of the snaps Sunday, Jacory Croskey-Merritt played 57 percent with 19 carries, and Austin Ekeler made the trip after signing Monday. Croskey-Merritt is the start either way. Monitor White; Thursday's practice report from London.

Jayden Daniels (WAS) was limited in Wednesday's 60-minute jog-through in London, his first practice since he dislocated the left elbow in Week 2, and Dan Quinn says the team will have a definite determination by Friday. Marcus Mariota took every snap vs SEA and threw 3 touchdowns, and he is the WAS quarterback on this week's Menu. Monitor Daniels; Friday's designation.

Mike Evans (SF) will not practice Wednesday while he manages the rib injury from ARI, and Kyle Shanahan says he expects him to play vs DEN. Trent Williams takes a rest day for the stinger and is expected back Thursday. Evans sits outside the ranked depth on the Menu until he practices. Monitor Evans; Thursday's practice.

Mike Vrabel says Drake Maye (NE) stays the starter @BUF after the fourth-quarter benching for Tommy DeVito: 1 touchdown pass, 6 interceptions and 7 turnovers in three games with A.J. Brown on IR. Maye is QB9 on this week's Menu, so the job, not the tape, is the call. Start him as your QB1.

Josh Oliver (MIN) went on injured reserve Tuesday with a torn biceps, so T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew are the only tight ends on the roster. Hockenson ran a route on 29 of 37 dropbacks vs TB and got 2 of the 4 targets for 11 yards, even with Justin Jefferson out from the first quarter. More snaps, same targets. Sit Hockenson vs MIA for any Menu tight end.

Rico Dowdle (PIT) did not practice Tuesday, his second straight missed session on the short week, and he has not practiced since he hurt the toe. Jaylen Warren played 90 percent of the snaps and touched the ball 20 times without him. Start Warren as your RB2 vs CLE Thursday.
The Giants released Odell Beckham Jr. Tuesday after 19 snaps, one target and no catches in three games, and signed Braxton Berrios to the active roster in his place. Drop him.

Tampa Bay signed Brett Rypien to the practice squad Tuesday, and Todd Bowles says undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels still starts vs GB. Daniels went 0 for 3 with an interception in relief of Baker Mayfield. Sit him in every format; he is not a streamer.

items.watch: Wednesday and Thursday practice reports from London
items.text: Jayden Daniels (WAS) flew to London with the team Tuesday night and is set to practice Wednesday through Friday in an elbow brace, per Dan Quinn. Washington decides on him vs IND after it sees him work. Monitor the Wednesday and Thursday practice reports.

items.watch: Wednesday practice; a full session is the tell
items.text: Sean McVay says he is hopeful Puka Nacua (LAR) plays at PHI after two missed games with groin soreness, and calls it to be determined. Terrance Ferguson and Jaylen Watson are likely out and Colby Parkinson's shoulder is undecided. Monitor Wednesday's practice; a full session is the tell.
Dave Canales says Jalen Coker (CAR) has a minor quad strain, and the team calls him questionable for DET. Monitor Wednesday's practice before you plug him in.

Roman Wilson (PIT) was benched for the second half vs CIN after a drop that became an interception, 2 snaps after halftime, so he comes off the Market Run adds list. Monitor his first-half snap share vs CLE Thursday before you spend.
items.watch: first-half snap share vs CLE Thursday

items.text: Ollie Gordon II (MIA) took 84 percent of the snaps after Achane went down, with a fullback and a receiver taking the other 12 at halfback. Miami worked out four backs Tuesday and signed none. Claim him, 20 to 30 percent of FAAB.
Jaylen Wright (MIA) sat Week 3 with a stinger and a foot issue, and Miami's coach said Monday he is day-to-day and could practice Wednesday. Stash him, 5 to 10 percent of FAAB.

Travis Etienne Jr. (NO) had 13 carries for 57 yards before the hamstring went, and Alvin Kamara took 6 of the next 10 carries and 20 of the 34 second-half snaps with CJ Donaldson on third downs. Claim Kamara, 15 to 25 percent of FAAB.

Kenyon Sadiq (NYJ) had three pass catchers out at DET, not one: Mason Taylor (thumb), Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper Jr. (IR). He ran a route on 58 percent of dropbacks and drew 21.6 percent of the targets. Claim him, 12 to 20 percent of FAAB.

The Market Run's Monday night note no longer calls Tyson Bagent the likely starter: Ben Johnson has not named one and said the staff will discuss it. Monitor who takes first-team reps at Wednesday practice.
items.watch: who takes first-team reps at Wednesday practice

items.text: Rashee Rice (KC) drew 9 of the Chiefs' 22 targets @MIA in Week 3, a 41 percent share, after 9.5 percent through two games. This week's Heat Check listed 18.7 percent as his Week 3 share; that is his three-game share, and the card is fixed. The buy call stands: trade for him, offer a WR3 and a bench RB.
items.price: a WR3 and a bench RB

items.text: D'Andre Swift (CHI) carried 20 times for 84 yards against his old team Monday night. Twenty carries is the number that matters. Start him as your RB2 vs NYJ.
Saquon Barkley (PHI) ran 15 times for 82 yards @CHI, 73 of them on 11 first-half carries before the game got away. Start him vs LAR.
